lead: A live formalization map makes unfinished dependencies visible, while reactions and complexity commentary cannot settle the underlying mathematical claims. Local tools disclose network paths, and a small model comparison keeps a near-tied score separate from the cost of one consequential error.

The late-morning batch adds an explicitly AI-written disclosure essay, a reading of OpenAI's loss chart and pressure on infrastructure from organizing and reported controls. Financing, strategic-risk scenarios and a hobby driving demo keep their source and testing limits.

The afternoon brings a material change in mathematical evidence: a joint Lean/Mathlib certification and an independent verification register for Alpöge. NVIDIA restores Huang while retaining its inquiry. New capability evaluations, model releases and infrastructure deals keep tested results, company claims and forecasts separate.

The night batch adds computer-use experiments, low-bit model results and an alpha browser with explicit security limits. Code-review delegation, local CRM and an AWS safety essay are recorded as product descriptions and arguments, not instructions to alter this workflow.

Runtime defense, code approval and cross-request safety monitoring expose distinct enforcement and data-custody questions. A dated places benchmark makes grading limits visible; product rollouts, investment automation and legal reporting keep claims separate from verified outcomes.

The late-morning batch tests the boundary between verifiable code properties and general correctness. A UK agent rollout, provider-data incidents and competing accounts of AI economics retain source-specific limits; an inaccessible interview is not reconstructed.

The afternoon batch separates a major algebraic-complexity claim from verified quantum resource reductions. Customer interviews, messy-workplace benchmarks and internal safety reporting probe different limits of agent deployment; market reactions and corporate transactions retain their dated, source-specific scope.

The evening batch adds desktop-app permissions, a sandbox honeypot and protein-design experiments with different verification boundaries. A signed New York moratorium and Tidal's announced music policy retain their scope and timing; forum accounts, market coverage and political commentary do not substitute for audited outcomes.

A new matrix-multiplication manuscript makes an arithmetic-exponent claim, while a model-ranked problem directory makes its own uncertainty explicit. Small generative models, archival research and systems essays retain experimental and case-study limits; market reporting distinguishes estimates, transactions and forecasts.

The late-morning update adds a scoped arithmetic-complexity preprint, a Dutch warning on camera-glasses safety and a local-backup product with explicit data-flow limits. Shopping-agent access talks remain unresolved, while financing reports distinguish a completed round from a proposed investment ceiling.

The afternoon batch puts agent performance in context: restarts complicate swarm claims, legal rubric gains can diverge from preference, and serving comparisons depend on detailed settings. Voice recreation, camera glasses and product rollouts raise distinct consent, safety and availability questions; credit and market stories retain their limited evidence.

The late update closes a genuine verification milestone: MIT reports the final check of the original RH artifact complete, while a separate abbreviated repository keeps its own limits. Production migration, code golf, creative work and local software illustrate different standards of evidence; toy rules and financing stories retain date, scope and completion distinctions.

The first update separates two ChatGPT usage changes and reports a proposed sale of sensitive chatbot data under legal challenge. Directly confirmed photography guidance, child-safety reporting and hardware tracing keep their scopes explicit; bare-metal inference and desktop wrappers remain demonstrations with different dependencies.

The late-morning update pairs concrete human review of generated expressions with competing accounts of AI privacy and security. Market rotation, memory shortages and reported shipment restrictions remain dated observations rather than universal conclusions; vendor offers and personal complaints keep their evidence limits visible.

The afternoon adds primary-grounded Google access-policy reporting, evaluation results with clear setting limits, and tools for historical retrieval and approximate model-state transfer. Rumored releases and broad mathematical claims remain separated from verified identity, independent proof checking and account-level availability.

The evening adds a reported Z.ai denial that leaves its release timing contested, and separates infrastructure enthusiasm from deskilling concerns. Backup tools, local dictation, bank risk transfers and a proposed SAP restructuring keep their privacy, execution and evidentiary boundaries explicit.

The first update separates bounded agent research from recursive self-improvement and a bubble-state estimate from an imminent-crash prediction. Product monitoring, authorship detection and legislative proposals keep their claims and evidence limits distinct.

The late-morning update separates fictional AI gossip and sampled personas from claims about model intentions. A research-sabotage allegation remains unverified, while European tooling advocacy and Taiwanese stock outflows keep their dates, sources and decision limits explicit.

The afternoon separates actual evaluation-boundary failures from speculation about cryptography and self-improvement. Research proposals, vendor efficiency results and payment trials retain their verification, compute, permission and legal boundaries; unreleased interfaces stay unreleased.

The evening adds competing forecasts, a primary tensor preprint and reports on copyright payments and a countersuit. It keeps subjective probabilities, legal allegations, partial profiles and product claims separate from verified outcomes, while revisiting sabotage claims without assuming intent.
